name: Telephony and Contact-Centre Integration
question: How does a voice agent plug into real phone lines and a contact centre?
summary: A voice agent in a lab talks to a browser microphone; in production it must answer phone calls. Calls arrive over the public phone network or a SIP trunk from a provider such as Exotel, Plivo or Twilio, and the provider streams 8 kHz audio to the agent over a WebSocket or bridges it into a media server such as LiveKit. The agent needs call control (answer, hold, DTMF keypad input, hang up), a warm transfer that passes a summary to a human agent in the contact centre, call recording with consent, and logging into the CRM. In India, media routed through distant regions adds delay, and outbound calling must follow TRAI’s commercial-communication rules, including do-not-disturb preferences and designated number series. This is an educational summary; confirm current telecom rules. Latency budgets and speech models are covered by the Voice Agents and Speech in Indian Languages techniques.
useCases: Inbound helplines moving from IVR menus to voice agents
Contact centres that blend bots and human agents

steps.title: Answer the call
steps.text: Dhan Seva, a fictional NBFC, points its provider’s webhook at /incoming, which tells the provider to stream the call audio to the agent.

steps.title: Stream the audio
steps.text: Audio arrives as 8 kHz μ-law frames over a WebSocket; the session runs speech-to-text, the agent and Hindi text-to-speech on the stream.

steps.title: Handle the keypad
steps.text: Callers can still press keys: DTMF digits reach the agent, useful for entering a loan number or choosing a language.

steps.title: Transfer warm
steps.text: When the caller wants a person or the agent is unsure, it hands the call to the loans queue with a summary: intent, loan id and whether the caller was verified.

steps.title: Log and record with consent
steps.text: Every call is logged to the CRM with its transcript; recording happens only after the consent notice.

steps.title: Keep media near callers
steps.text: With media in a Mumbai region, replies start in about 700 ms instead of 950 ms. Outbound calls are scrubbed against DND preferences and use the approved number series.

practice.scenario: Dhan Seva, a fictional NBFC, gets 40,000 loan-status calls a month. Its IVR resolved 20% and every transfer made callers repeat themselves. It now answers with a voice agent over an Indian telephony provider’s media stream processed in Mumbai, handles keypad input, and transfers to the loans queue with a summary. 55% of calls are resolved on the call, replies start in about 700 ms, human handle time falls from 300 to 190 seconds, and cost per call drops from ₹22 to about ₹13.

industries.use: Claim-status calls in Hindi and regional languages

practice.analogy: A receptionist who answers the phone, sorts most questions on the spot, and when handing over to a colleague says “this is Mr Sharma, loan 4471, already verified” instead of just putting the call through.

library.name: FastAPI
library.what: A small FastAPI server receives the provider’s webhook and the audio WebSocket.

practice.note: Message fields follow Twilio Media Streams; Exotel and Plivo use similar JSON events. The voice session is a placeholder for your STT → agent → TTS pipeline (for example Pipecat).

samples.code:
import base64, json
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()

@app.websocket("/media")
async def media(ws: WebSocket):
    await ws.accept()
    frames = 0
    async for raw in ws.iter_text():
        msg = json.loads(raw)
        if msg["event"] == "start":
            print("call", msg["start"]["callSid"])
        elif msg["event"] == "media":
            audio = base64.b64decode(msg["media"]["payload"])   # 8 kHz mu-law, 20 ms
            frames += 1                                           # feed your STT here
        elif msg["event"] == "stop":
            print("frames:", frames, "seconds:", frames * 0.02)
            break

interview.question: How do you connect a voice agent to real phone calls?
interview.answer: Use a telephony provider with numbers or a SIP trunk, stream call audio (8 kHz μ-law) to the agent over a WebSocket or bridge SIP into a media server, handle DTMF, hold and hang-up, transfer warm to the contact centre with a summary, and log to the CRM.

interview.question: What is a warm transfer?
interview.answer: Handing a call to a human along with context, such as intent, account and verification status, so the caller does not repeat themselves.
